stdout_tail:
This looks correct and complete. Both `analysis.py` and `result.json` are saved.

**Finding:** The RandomForestClassifier (300 trees, default depth, one-hot encoded categoricals) trained on a stratified 70/30 split is **well-calibrated** on held-out test data — Expected Calibration Error (10-bin) = 0.0159, Brier score = 0.1003. Predicted probabilities track observed frequencies closely across almost all bins (mean predicted 0.239 vs. actual base rate 0.239 overall); the largest local gap is in the 0.5–0.6 predicted-probability bin (predicted 0.55 vs. observed 0.48). A logistic regression reference model is calibrated even more tightly (ECE = 0.0088), but both land comfortably in the "well-calibrated" range, so miscalibration doesn't appear to be a meaningful concern for this dataset/model combination.

parsed_result.summary: The primary model (RandomForestClassifier) is well-calibrated overall on the held-out test set, with an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.0159 and Brier score of 0.1003; predicted probabilities track observed frequencies closely in most bins, with the largest local deviation in the [0.5, 0.6] predicted-probability bin (predicted 0.55 vs. observed 0.48). A logistic regression reference model is even better calibrated (ECE=0.0088), but both models fall in the 'well-calibrated' range under the threshold used here.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Expected Calibration Error (10-bin, RandomForest, test set)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Target binarized as class=='>50K'. Missing categorical values filled with an explicit 'Missing' category (no rows dropped); no missingness in numeric columns. Single stratified 70/30 train/test split (random_state=42), no cross-validation. Primary model: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=300, default depth) with one-hot encoded categoricals and raw numeric features. Reference model: LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000) with the same one-hot encoding plus StandardScaler on numeric features. No class-imbalance correction applied (class_weight=None) — base rate of '>50K' is ~24%, which is used as the calibration reference point. Calibration measured via Expected Calibration Error (10 equal-width bins on predicted probability) as the primary metric, with Brier score and a full reliability table reported as supporting evidence. Thresholds for the well/mildly/materially calibrated verdict (ECE<0.02 / <0.05 / >=0.05) are a subjective judgment call, not a standard convention. No post-hoc recalibration (e.g. Platt scaling, isotonic regression) was applied — the question asks about calibration of the fitted model as-is.
